papers.title: AtumAI: A Principled Framework for Agentic Generation of Datacenter Control-Plane Policies

history.note: arXiv v1 (submitted 2026-08-03) presents a task compiler plus evolutionary design loop evaluated on workload placement, resource scaling, and power management; the paper reports 17% placement-success, 24% cost-efficiency, and 21% power reductions versus expert baselines, but no code or data artifact was identified.

papers.title: Real-Time Detection and Repair of LLM Agent Failures

history.note: arXiv v1 (submitted 2026-08-03) reports 2,823 committed episodes across three frameworks and four model families, releases code/traces/results, and combines a low-cost temporal monitor with deterministic verification and rollback repair. The artifact also documents cold-start, selection, and hallucination limits.
Prepared the bilingual deep read as 14-agent-trajectory-sentinel after subagent drafting and main review; retains the monitor/verification/repair distinction and artifact limitations.

papers.title: Before Reasoning Fails: Pre-Evidence Procedural Failures in Agentic RAG

history.note: arXiv v1 (submitted 2026-08-03) decomposes 12,000 paired trajectories across HotpotQA, 2WikiMultiHopQA, and MuSiQue into pre-evidence and post-read failures, then evaluates a Read-Gate intervention. Code is linked from the paper; domain scope is Wikipedia-style multi-hop QA and API-based controllers.
Prepared the bilingual deep read as 15-before-reasoning-fails after subagent drafting and main review, pinned to the cited v1 evidence; arXiv now exposes v2 and requires a future version recheck.

papers.title: HALT: Verification-Aware Stopping for Retrieval-Augmented Search Agents

history.note: Same-author companion to arxiv:2608.02011. The paper and official repository report evidence-coverage stopping, 6-9% loop reduction for generated claims, and 19-45% in gold-claim diagnostics while preserving exact match in most tested cells. Keep as a follow-up rather than a second Deep Read until independent or broader-domain evidence is available.

papers.title: PAST-Bench: Benchmarking the Foundations of Recursive Self-Improvement in Personal Agents

history.note: arXiv v1 submitted 2026-08-04 presents 26 task families and 204 fresh-session episodes across memory, procedural reuse, information gathering, and update, with matched persistence-on/off controls and trace-level mechanism evidence across seven models and four agent frameworks. The official repository is available under Apache-2.0; external model and framework dependencies remain practical reproduction constraints.
Prepared the bilingual deep read as 16-past-bench-recursive-self-improvement after subagent drafting and main review; preserves matched controls, trace-level evidence, and reproduction constraints.

papers.title: Training Documents Reranker with Search Rubrics for Deep Research Agent

history.note: arXiv v1 submitted 2026-08-04 proposes rubric-guided SFT plus rubric-based GRPO for set-level document selection, reporting a 2.6-point gain over the strongest baseline on four deep-research benchmarks and generalization to five RAG benchmarks. The official repository, MIT-licensed code, ModelScope model, and SFT/RL data are available; evaluation uses sampled queries and LLM judges.

Prepared the bilingual deep read as 17-rubric-ranker-deep-research through main-author review; reproduces the paper tables and figures while separating official artifact availability from claims that still need download verification.

papers.title: MAFIA: Query-Only Memory Attacks via Probing and Factual Injection against Audited LLM Agents

history.note: arXiv v1 submitted 2026-08-04 studies query-only poisoning of similarity-retrieved agent memory across four agent-dataset configurations, with ablations and audit-defense analysis. The paper reports up to 90.7% attack success and at most 7.4% audit detection in its tested setting, but the official repository still says code release is in preparation and the scope excludes graph or hierarchical memory. Keep as a security shortlist item pending artifact release and responsible-reading review.

papers.title: TARL: Transaction-Aware Reliable Ledgers for Executable Memory Management in Long-Term Agents

history.note: arXiv v1 submitted 2026-08-04 defines five executable memory-update actions and the 5,422-example TARL-Mem benchmark derived from HaluMem, LoCoMo, and LongMemEval, with extensive controlled evaluation. The paper says complete code, data, and reproduction materials will be released with final publication; keep as a shortlist extension of the existing agent-memory path until artifacts and scope are independently checked.

papers.title: ContextWeave: A Real-World Workflow Benchmark

history.note: arXiv v1 submitted 2026-08-05 evaluates memory in privacy-preserved multi-month workflows from 14 participants, reconstructing 1,005 executable tasks with 568 core tasks, containerized environments, and with-recall versus no-recall controls. The official OpenMOSS/ContextWeave repository includes code, data archive, Docker workflow, metrics, and reproduction instructions; rubric calibration and full-run cost remain limitations.

Prepared the bilingual deep read as 09-contextweave-workflow-benchmark with paper Figure 1–2 attribution, Table 1–2 result anchors, memory-induced risk analysis, and conditional artifact/reproducibility notes.

papers.title: Argus: A General-Purpose Agentic Runtime for Long-Horizon Reasoning

history.note: arXiv v1 submitted 2026-08-05 presents a Manager-Planner-Engineer-Reviewer runtime over bounded missions and durable state, with verification-gated objective revision and runtime self-evolution. The report spans seven task-native arenas plus longitudinal SWE-Bench and paper-production traces; no public Argus implementation or trace package was identified, while an independently merged RWKV6 kernel PR provides a downstream artifact.

Prepared the bilingual deep read as 10-argus-agentic-runtime with paper Figure 1–4 attribution, task-native versus longitudinal evidence separation, downstream artifact caveat, and authority/verifier/rollback engineering guidance.

papers.title: Architectural Implications of Agentic AI Workflows

history.note: arXiv v1 submitted 2026-08-05 combines a Microsoft Azure production study with controlled open-source framework experiments and introduces Agora for role-aware CPU harvesting, GPU consolidation, and tail-latency protection. The engineering evidence is strong, but no public artifact was identified and the paper is infrastructure characterization rather than a direct coordination method; retain as a shortlist companion to an AI-platform or runtime path.

papers.title: The Bitter Lesson of Tool Calling

history.note: Seven-day backfill verified arXiv v1 submitted 2026-08-06. The paper compares JSON and programmatic tool calling across 14 models on 309 BFCL v4 entries, with chaining, parallelism, and context-rot ablations; it reports 11/14 match-or-exceed results and 10.6-point GPT-5.6-Sol/Terra gains. The paper-specific harness and full cost trace remain unknown.
